notes:
SCOPE AND LIMITS. This file ranks the US manufacturing plants for which a site headcount could be sourced on 18 November 2026. It is not a complete top 100. Web search stopped working part-way through (the session's shared search budget ran out), so after the first 30 or so plants every figure came from pages reached directly: company and newsroom pages, city financial reports, economic development lists, and Wikipedia. 99 plants are ranked and 2 more are in `unplaced`; roughly the first 60 ranks are plants that belong in a national top 100, while the lower ranks are plants that happened to have a figure, and many larger plants are missing (listed below). Treat `rank` as the order within this file.

HOW TO READ THE SOURCES. 42 plants carry a figure seen on a company, government or news page. 57 carry a figure read on Wikipedia only (their `employeesSource` is a wikipedia.org URL and `employeesNote` begins "Read on Wikipedia only"); most of those trace to a city's annual financial report (principal employers table) or to a Ford, GM or Stellantis plant page that is now blocked to automated requests or no longer states employment. Those 57 should be re-checked against a primary source before they are shown as fact. A city report's figure is the employer's headcount in that city, which for a few entries covers more than the factory floor (see the notes on Tesla Fremont, Boeing St. Louis, Boeing El Segundo, JBS Greeley, Hormel Austin, GE Appliance Park, Gulfstream, Micron Boise).

JUDGMENT CALLS. (1) Campuses reported as one: Intel Oregon (four Hillsboro-area campuses, mapped at Ronler Acres), Intel in Chandler (two campuses, mapped at Ocotillo), Textron Aviation Wichita (east and west campuses about 12 miles apart, mapped at the west campus), Boeing St. Louis (Lambert airport plant plus St. Charles and offices), John Deere Waterloo Works (several sites in Waterloo), L3Harris Rochester, ADM Decatur. (2) Sites where engineering or headquarters staff are a large share of the count: Boeing Everett, Lockheed Martin Fort Worth, Gulfstream, Raytheon Tucson, Boeing St. Louis, Boeing El Segundo (a satellite factory inside an engineering campus: the weakest fit for "plant" in the top 20), Pratt & Whitney East Hartford, Micron Boise (headquarters and research fab; the production fab is still being built), SpaceX Hawthorne, Lockheed Martin Grand Prairie and Sunnyvale, Eastman Kingsport. (3) Boeing Wichita is the former Spirit AeroSystems plant, owned by Boeing since December 2025; "Spirit AeroSystems" is listed under Boeing's alsoKnownAs for that reason, but Spirit's other former sites did not all go to Boeing, so merge by place. (4) Rivian Normal uses the Illinois headcount Rivian reported to the state (7,410, May 2025) because Rivian no longer gives a plant figure. (5) Gigafactory Nevada uses the state's count of qualified employees on the site (Tesla plus Panasonic and H&T), which understates the people on site. (6) Volkswagen Chattanooga's 3,200 is the hourly bargaining unit only. (7) Hyundai Metaplant: "nearly 2,000" (company, June 2026) was used over Wikipedia's "3,200+". (8) Sikorsky Stratford uses the town's 5,734 over a local paper's 7,900. (9) Old figures kept because nothing newer could be reached: National Beef Liberal (2011), Pfizer Rocky Mount (2018), Goodyear Fayetteville (2018), ExxonMobil Beaumont (2018), Smithfield Tar Heel (2008, unplaced). (10) Detroit Assembly Complex is kept as its two plants, Jefferson and Mack, as Stellantis reports them.

CONFLICTING FIGURES (the other figure is in each plant's employeesNote): Tesla Fremont 25,000 (city, 2024) against "over 20,000" (2023); Giga Texas 16,506 (2025) against 21,191 (2024); Raytheon Tucson "nearly 13,000" (2026) against the city's 9,600 (2023); Boeing Wichita 13,000 against 9,500 for Spirit in March 2025; Textron Aviation 11,000 against 9,000; Arlington Assembly 5,641 (2022) against the city's 8,919 for GM (2024); Intel Chandler 11,000 (2025) against 12,000 (2024); Hyundai Alabama 4,200 (company) against Montgomery's 3,530 (2022).

LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE. Government-owned nuclear weapons plants run by contractors (Kansas City National Security Campus, Pantex, Y-12; Wikipedia gives Y-12 8,600, undated): they are production plants, but government-owned, and no dated site figure was reachable; the owner should decide whether they belong. GM's Warren Technical Center (21,000, engineering), Lilly's Indianapolis campus and other headquarters or research campuses are not plants. Tyson's Lexington, Nebraska beef plant (3,200) closed in January 2026. BlueOval SK's Kentucky battery plant (about 1,600 to 1,700 people in December 2025) was laying off its workforce for retooling. Electric Boat's Quonset Point yard has no site figure: Electric Boat as a whole had about 25,000 employees in February 2026 (https://portal.ct.gov/oma/in-the-news/2026-news/eb-to-hire-8000-this-year).
